transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-29 16:00 PDT
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Marissa Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Patel (Redwood SE), Oliver Grant (Redwood CSM), Rhea Morales (Redwood Product), Alex Moreno (CTO, Argonautica), Priya Singh (Infra Eng), Sam Lewis (Security), Dana Ortiz (Product Ops), Miguel Torres (Finance)

--- Auto-generated summary (may be rough) ---
Argonautica is ramping to GA for their recommendation engine mid-September; they have a big spike risk around a marketing event in late August. Primary asks: keep 95/99 latency under 400/700ms for short chat flows, and keep per-month inference spend within the committed budget. They want a canary on Dedicated and checks for KMS/audit.

00:00:05 Marissa (AE): Hey folks, thanks for carving this hour — goal today is to align on capacity forecast and the stability playbook before your August marketing spike. Quick intros?
00:00:16 Alex (CTO): Alex here, CTO. Priya is infra, Sam security, Dana product ops, Miguel finance.
00:00:24 Priya (Infra): Hi, yep.
00:00:26 Marissa: Great. Devon, quick overview from your side?
00:00:29 Devon (SE): Yeah hi—I'll walk through what we've seen in the baseline metrics and where the cost is coming from. I pulled your last 45 days of calls, mostly short-turn Q&A, plus some longer batch re-ranks. Noticed heavy token variance on peak hours and a ~20% slow tail beyond 500ms that spikes cost.
00:00:49 Miguel (Finance): When you say tail, is that because of long prompts? Or is it model selection?
00:00:55 Devon: A mix. We see a small percent of long prompts and a lot of cold KV cache misses — the KV cash, sorry, kv cash — kv cache is the thing — yeah, cold cache. So per-token compute jumps. Also we suspect model fallbacks from larger backbone occasionally add cost.
00:01:12 Sam (Security): Can you clarify what data leaves our VPC for hosted? We need proof for PII flows.
00:01:18 Marissa: Good call — Argonautica is still on hosted for the prototype, right? We discussed Dedicated earlier as a path to reduce egress and have isolation.
00:01:25 Alex: Hosted for now, but we are evaluating Dedicated — main blocker is the procurement and whether we can encrypt keys with our HSM through KMS integration.
00:01:34 Rhea (Product): Also want to make sure accuracy doesn't regress if we switch to a smaller quantized variant.
00:01:38 Devon: Totally. We'll provide quality delta guidance per model/quant level. For the stability playbook I want to propose three levers: caching (prefix + KV), smarter routing to cheaper variants during non-critical windows, and burstable Dedicated pool to handle marketing spikes.
00:01:53 Dana (Product Ops): Burstable dedicated — how fast is that really? If we flip it on for a campaign, can it ramp in minutes?
00:02:00 Marissa: Typically minutes for warm instances if we keep a small standby. For full scale we recommend a 24–48 hour prep window for graceful prefetching of KV/caches. The burst capacity is configurable — there's a cost hit but less than sustained overprovisioning.
00:02:16 Priya: Ok, so operationally we need to decide what prefix caches we persist across restarts. We can't keep unbounded state in local GPU. How does Redwood handle that?
00:02:25 Devon: We persist warm prefixes in a distributed cache and back them with a small, pre-warmed embedding table. There is a tradeoff between cache size and miss-rate; we'll show you a simulation using your prompt set.
00:02:34 Alex: Simulation would be great. Also Miguel — what's our comfortable upper bound monthly spend?
00:02:39 Miguel: We can push 35% over baseline for one month but can't sustain it long-term. The board gave us a runway but they want clear guardrails.
00:02:47 Marissa: Perfect — that informs the guardrail thresholds. Suggest we set two cost policies: soft alert at +20% and hard throttle at +40% with automatic fallbacks to cached responses or smaller variants.
00:02:58 Sam: For compliance, will those fallbacks leak anything? If we switch to a smaller variant, is there a change in logging or audit retention?
00:03:05 Devon: No, logging is the same; trace IDs persist. The model variant is metadata only. We can also add a policy to block fallback for flows marked PII/sensitive.
00:03:14 Sam: Good. We need that whitelist.
00:03:17 Alex: Let's talk SLOs — 95/99 targets I mentioned earlier are for our customer-facing chat; background batch re-ranks can have higher latency. Can you map cost to hitting 95/99?
00:03:27 Devon: Yes. In general for your profile: hitting 95 at ~350ms maps to a particular kernel selection and batch size 8; 99 tails are where kv-cache and prefetching matter. If we keep a dedicated pool for short contexts we can tighten tail latency; that increases base cost but reduces per-request variance.
00:03:44 Dana: Anything we can do on product side to reduce the slow tail? E.g., prompt trimming?
00:03:48 Rhea: We have some pre-processing we can do to normalize prompts. We can also nudge UX to split long flows.
00:03:53 Marissa: Great, actions there.
00:03:55 Alex: Procurement — timeline question: if we decide dedicated, how long is lead time for contract and provisioning?
00:04:02 Marissa: Contract is usually 2–4 weeks for a reserved commit, provisioning depends on pool size but can be done in 48–72 hours for initial sizing. For on-prem/VPC connect there's an extra setup week.
00:04:13 Priya: On KMS — we use CloudHSM. Can Redwood integrate with external HSM for key wrapping?
00:04:20 Devon: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations; we'll need an integration engineer on your side to exchange endpoint info and certs. We've done CloudHSM and vendor-specific HSMs.
00:04:30 Sam: We'll want to validate with a pen-test of the connectivity.
00:04:34 Marissa: Noted. We'll include a security runbook and SAML/SOAR details.
00:04:38 Miguel: Back to cost — can you show a committed vs on-demand cost table?
00:04:42 Marissa: We'll send two CSVs: one baseline hosted, and one for a small dedicated pool with burst configuration. We'll include a 6-month projection for the spike month.
00:04:52 Alex: Good. Also want a test where you replay our August expected load with 10% longer tail to see where queueing appears.
00:04:59 Devon: We'll run a synthetic replay on a dedicated staging pool — that will give us tail profiles and the first-failure points. We should plan that for 2026-07-15.
00:05:09 Dana: Who owns the run? Redwood? Or we share credentials?
00:05:13 Marissa: Redwood can run the replay if you provide anonymized traffic and a staging key. Alternatively we can provide a script and you run it.
00:05:20 Priya: We'll want to run it in our VPC-connected staging for realistic networking.
00:05:24 Devon: That's preferable — network variance matters. We'll help set it up.
00:05:28 Alex: Ok. Let's talk postmortem of last month's incident — there was a period where 5% of requests got a model fallback and we saw 3x cost. What changed?
00:05:37 Oliver (CSM): I pulled the logs — looks like a sudden routing change to a larger model variant to recover from a transient GPU OOM. Redwood's automatic fallback selected a larger replica which briefly drove cost. We've added a config option to prefer same-size variant fallback or regional fallback instead.
00:05:52 Marissa: That setting is important — we'll suggest prefer-regional-smaller-variant to avoid cost shock.
00:05:56 Alex: Can we add runbook steps so our on-call can identify and flip the routing policy?
00:06:01 Devon: Yes. We'll add a minimal UI doc and an API toggle.
00:06:04 Sam: For audit, we need a log of any automated fallback action for the prior 90 days. Is that available?
00:06:09 Devon: Yes, it's available in the console and can be exported. We'll include a sample export.
00:06:13 Miguel: Pricing — if we do a 12-month reserved capacity, what is the break-even vs on-demand?
00:06:18 Marissa: For your expected baseline, a 12-month commit with 20% headroom saves roughly 18–22% compared to pure on-demand. We'll model three tiers in the sheet.
00:06:27 Alex: Alright. Next item — quality monitoring. We want alerts if output divergence increases after a quant/variant swap.
00:06:34 Rhea: We can wire a small eval harness to run key prompts hourly and get a regression score. If quality drops beyond threshold we can auto rollback.
00:06:40 Dana: That would be fantastic — automated rollback on regression is a must for us.
00:06:44 Devon: We'll propose a rollout policy: canary 5% for 48h, 25% for 48h, then full if quality stable. Canary runs will be against pinned prompt sets.
00:06:53 Marissa: Great. I'll include rollout policy language in the follow-up.
00:06:56 Priya: A quick security note — we need to ensure logs don't include PII. If fallback happens, do logs redact differently?
00:07:02 Devon: Redaction is consistent; we also offer token-level redaction rules. We'll share the docs.
00:07:06 Sam: We'll review the token redaction rules; also want a timeline for SOC2 artifacts.
00:07:10 Marissa: We'll attach SOC2 and ISO artifacts and a short mapping doc to your security questionnaire by 2026-07-02.
00:07:16 Alex: Good. Any blockers on your side, Priya?
00:07:19 Priya: We need the KMS contact info and the staging network CIDR to set firewall rules.
00:07:24 Marissa: Noted — action item for Priya to share; Devon will coordinate.
00:07:28 Miguel: Final question: what's the suggested minimal Dedicated pool size for our traffic?
00:07:33 Devon: Based on the last 45 days with a 2x marketing spike, I'd recommend a dual-pool: small steady pool sized at 60% of peak and a burst pool at 40% that stays cold-but-prewarmed. That gives decent tail coverage without 100% overprovision. Exact numbers in the forecast sheet.
00:07:49 Alex: Sounds reasonable. Any other open asks?
00:07:52 Dana: Can we get a short written playbook for the on-call to follow during a spike?
00:07:56 Marissa: We'll include a short Ops playbook (2 pages) with escalation flow, throttles, rollback steps, and where to find logs.
00:08:04 Oliver: And we'll set a follow-up checkpoint 1 week after you review the spreadsheet to lock in dates.
00:08:09 Marissa: Awesome. Quick recap of next steps and owners?
00:08:12 Marissa (AE): Action items recap: I will send pricing/capacity CSV and SOC2 artifacts by 2026-07-02. Devon will run a cache/prefix simulation and the synthetic replay plan will be ready for 2026-07-08. Priya to share KMS contact and staging CIDR by 2026-07-05. Sam to hand over security questions by 2026-07-06. We also scheduled the canary replay for 2026-07-15.
00:08:34 Alex: Thanks everyone. That covers it. We'll look at the spreadsheets and pick the commit band.
00:08:39 Marissa: Thanks all — end meeting.
